ruling.recommended_action: Hold the fare-dispute decision; send to a human reviewer to match the driver's GPS trace against the road network (name the roads on both the agreed Rifle Range Road stretch and the later off-route loop) before any RydeTAXI metered refund is computed under RD-2. + flag_account
ruling.reasoning:
RydeTAXI metered trip T-2013 (Woodlands Civic Centre → Orchard Road). Fare $61.32 is metered: 30.95 km billed vs 20.566 km quoted (≈10.4 km more), so any unexempt deviation feeds the fare (RD-2 taxi branch; distance rate $43.64/30.95 km = $1.41/km).

Chat: at 18:42:35 the driver said the BKE jam was building and proposed the named road "Rifle Range Road"; at 18:43:15 the rider replied "Sure, your call." That is consent to a specific named road, given before the segment (RD-5). But the trace between 18:42:25 and 18:52:25 runs north-west/south-west (lon ~103.775 → ~103.777 with lat near 1.34–1.36, an area tagged ~6–8 km from Rifle Range Road in the route corridor data) rather than south-west into the corridor; and the driver's own statement says the later turn-off was a GPS reroute, not the agreed road. The record therefore places part of that stretch away from Rifle Range Road — a named_road_elsewhere / driver_errand reading (counts) — while the rest cannot be tied to the agreed road at all (named_road_untied → undetermined, G12/G13). A second, separate off-route excursion appears at 19:03:55–19:12:25 (heading north-east away from the drop-off before returning), with no chat message before it: consent_after_or_none → counts (RD-5). No LTA incident is recorded, and the only speed bands are band 4, which cannot exempt under RD-4 (band ≤ 2 support only; G3).

The rider alleges she agreed only to the first detour; system records do not settle whether the driver's "go round via Rifle Range Road" consent covers the first detour segments or whether the second loop was a driver errand vs GPS reroute. Because segments whose finding is undetermined change the refund amount and the RD-6 account flag, the case cannot be executed automatically and goes to a human reviewer.
ruling.escalation_reason: RD-5 consent scope for the later off-route stretch is undetermined (G13) and this finding changes the refund amount and the RD-6 flag decision; a human reviewer must resolve the road correspondence before ruling.

segment_findings.reason: First post-consent stretch (GPS 18:42:25–18:52:25) leaves the BKE corridor right after the rider's "Sure, your call." at 18:43:15, which is consent to the driver's named road 'Rifle Range Road' (RD-5). Nothing in the thinned GPS trace (no road names) ties this driven stretch to Rifle Range Road, and the driver's statement only says 'the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting', so the scope is undetermined (G12/G13). An undetermined finding that changes the amount → escalate.

Second excursion (GPS 19:03:55–19:12:25) leaves the corridor heading north-east away from Orchard Road (lat 1.3317→1.3408, lon 103.8145→103.8340) then loops back, adding unauthorised mileage. No chat message precedes this segment and the rider only agreed to one diversion; the chat is complete, so no rider message was available and this is an unexcused deviation under RD-1/RD-5 (counts).

Opening stretch of the off-route run (GPS 18:45:25–18:52:25, lon ~103.775 pushing west/south-west while lat climbs 1.3637→1.3425) heads away from the rider's named road and away from the destination; the record places it away from the agreed named road and the driver's own account calls it a GPS reroute, not the agreed road, so the RD-5 named-road consent does not cover it (RD-5; counts).

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's claim of agreement is not itself consent (G11); the only rider consent on record is the 18:43:15 message 'Sure, your call.', which is tied to the named road Rifle Range Road and does not cover the later unannounced loop.

A driver's own GPS reroute is not a 'reasonable cause' under RD-4: no LTA traffic incident is recorded on the replaced optimal-route stretch, and the only speed bands are band 4, which cannot exempt (RD-4(b), G3).

ruling.evidence_gap: GPS trace is thinned (every 6th sample, 30 s grid) and carries no road names, and the record contains no road-name facts linking the driven off-route stretches to the agreed "Rifle Range Road"; the first off-route stretch (18:42:25–18:52:25) cannot be tied to the named road or definitively placed elsewhere, which prevents an executable RD-2 refund computation.
